$comment: Rules are matched in order; the first match wins. Paths are case-insensitive and %VARS% expand against the current environment. Edit freely - the app reads this file on every scan.

rules.reason: Component store used for Windows servicing. Removing it corrupts updates and repairs.
Core operating system binaries.
32-bit compatibility layer for the operating system.
MSI repair and uninstall data. Deleting it makes installed programs impossible to update or remove.
System restore and shadow copy data, owned by Windows.
Dependencies shipped inside an installed application. There is no package.json build step to restore them — deleting this breaks the app.
Dependencies shipped inside an installed application. Not regenerable.
Dependencies shipped inside a per-user installed application. Not regenerable.
Dependencies shipped inside an application installed under the Public profile. Not regenerable.
Dependencies inside shared application data. Uninstall the owning program instead.
Dependencies of a globally installed CLI. Deleting this breaks the command, and `npm install` at the project level will not restore it.
Dependencies of a Pinokio-managed app. Reinstalled only by Pinokio itself.
Hugging Face model downloads. Regenerable, but re-downloading them can cost many gigabytes.
PyTorch hub and compiled kernel cache. Regenerable but expensive to rebuild.
Whisper model downloads. Re-downloadable.
CapCut drafts and imported footage. This is your work, not cache.
A game save folder. Worlds and progress are not recoverable once deleted.
Screenshots you took in-game.
Minecraft worlds. Not recoverable once deleted.
Minecraft worlds managed by TLauncher. Not recoverable once deleted.
npm re-downloads packages on the next install.
npm content-addressable cache. Rebuilds itself.
pip wheels cache. Rebuilds on the next install.
Yarn global cache. Re-downloaded on demand.
Bun install cache. Re-downloaded on demand.
uv cache. Re-downloaded on demand.
Scratch space left behind by installers and apps.
Diagnostic dumps from crashed apps. Only useful when actively debugging.
Queued Windows Error Reporting data.
Legacy Internet Explorer / WebView cache.
Direct3D shader cache. Rebuilt by the driver on demand.
NVIDIA DirectX shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
NVIDIA OpenGL shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Squirrel installer staging area.
Downloaded installer for an app update that has already been applied.
Cached web content. Pages reload from the network.
Discord media cache. Re-downloaded as you browse.
Microsoft Teams cache. Rebuilt on restart.
Compiled Python bytecode. Regenerated on import.
pytest run cache. Regenerated on the next test run.
mypy type-check cache. Regenerated on the next run.
ruff lint cache. Regenerated on the next run.
Installed JS dependencies. Run `npm install` to recreate.
rules.impact: Project will not run until dependencies are reinstalled.

rules.reason: Per-tool cache directory (~/.cache). Tools rebuild their entries on demand. Large model downloads are excluded by the rules above.
Next.js build cache. Regenerated by `next build` or `next dev`.

CapCut render cache and previews — but this folder mixes regenerable scratch files (.yuv, .pcm, hash-named .mp4) with human-named exports, so it cannot be removed wholesale. Inspect the file list first.
CapCut app data beyond projects and cache - check what is inside before removing.
Claude Desktop local data and caches. Removing may sign you out and clear local history.
Downloaded model weights. Re-downloadable, but large - check which models you still use.
Arduino board cores and toolchains. Re-downloadable via the Board Manager.
Extracted NVIDIA driver packages. Windows does not need these once a driver is installed.
OEM driver packages left on disk after installation.
Autodesk installer cache and downloads. Only needed for repair or reinstall.
Per-app data for Store applications. Check the individual package before removing.
LDPlayer emulator images and Android data. Check for app data you want to keep.
Downloaded update packages. Safe to clear once updates are installed (needs administrator).
Playwright browser downloads. Re-installable with `npx playwright install`.
Globally installed npm packages. Deleting this uninstalls command-line tools you may rely on.
Cached installers used to repair or modify installed programs.
Your download folder. Nothing here is classified automatically - inspect it.
Coding-agent session logs, shell output and snapshots. Regenerable, but deletes your history.
Minecraft libraries and assets. Re-downloaded by the launcher if removed.
TLauncher libraries and assets. Re-downloaded on the next launch.
TLauncher library jars. Re-downloaded on the next launch.
Old Minecraft client versions kept by TLauncher. Re-downloadable; each one is large.
TLauncher app data. Game saves inside are protected and cannot be swept up with it.
Per-user installed applications. Uninstall through Settings rather than deleting.
Installed Xbox games. Remove through the Xbox app so licences stay intact.
Pinokio-installed apps and models.
Operating system files. Managed by Windows, not by this tool.
Shared application data. Uninstall the owning program instead.
Installed applications. Uninstall unused programs through Settings instead.
Installed applications. Uninstall unused programs through Settings instead.
Your video files.
Your images.
Your audio files.
Your documents.
Files on your desktop.
Locally cached OneDrive content. Manage it from OneDrive settings (Files On-Demand).
Inside your user profile. Inspect before removing anything.
